story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
1. Privacy policy page exists at the canonical project URL — implementation updates the existing German page at `content/pages/datenschutz.md` (resolved permalink `/pages/datenschutz/`) rather than creating a new page at `/pages/privacy/`. Reconciliation: site is German-language, file is already wired into footer menu, and creating a parallel English slug would split routing and break the legacy URL.
2. Policy explains the three engagement data flows: Umami (anonymous analytics), Hearts (Umami event tracking), and Webmentions (federated public engagement). Each flow gets a dedicated `##` section covering: what data is collected/received, where it is stored, the third-party processor (if any), the legal basis under DSGVO Art. 6, and how the reader can opt out. Coordination note: Story 2.3 AC #5 also adds a `## Webmentions` section — whichever lands first creates it; the second integrates without duplicating.
3. Policy explicitly states the privacy posture in a `## Was diese Seite NICHT tut` section: zero tracking cookies (Umami cookieless + Hearts via localStorage not cookies), no personal data collection (no signup/comments/newsletter), no third-party ads. Section also calls out existing third-party data exposures (GitHub Pages server-log, embedded YouTube via `youtube-nocookie.com`, webmention sender avatars loaded from third-party domains).
4. Policy is linked from the footer on every page — satisfied by existing footer-menu mechanism (`layouts/_partials/_base/footer.html` lines 73–87 render `.Site.Menus.footer`; `datenschutz.md` frontmatter `menu: footer: weight: 20`). No code change needed; verification is a regression check that rendered footer HTML still contains `Datenschutz` on a sample of pages.
5. Policy includes contact information for privacy questions — a dedicated `## Kontakt für Datenschutzanfragen` section with email obfuscated using the same anti-scraper pattern as `impressum.md` lines 19–24 (split with HTML comments and zero-width separator spans). Section explicitly enumerates the reader's DSGVO rights: Auskunft (Art. 15), Berichtigung (Art. 16), Löschung (Art. 17), Einschränkung (Art. 18), Datenübertragbarkeit (Art. 20), Widerspruch (Art. 21), Beschwerderecht (Art. 77).
6. Policy is dated and versioned. Two pieces of metadata after the title/intro: `Stand: TT.MM.JJJJ` (human-readable last-update date in German format; initial value at implementation = today) and `Version: X.Y` (semver-style; initial `1.0`; minor for additions, major for restructuring). Rendered as a small caption-style line below H1, e.g., `*Stand: 06. Mai 2026 · Version: 1.0*`. Adding `last_updated:`/`policy_version:` to frontmatter is also acceptable as long as the rendered page surfaces both values.
7. Outdated content is removed. The existing `## Spotify` section (lines 60–67) is removed — production codebase no longer contains Spotify embeds (grep returns zero matches in `layouts/`, `assets/`, `content/articles/`). The standalone `### Google Analytics und Google Web Fonts` one-liner is folded into the broader `## Was diese Seite NICHT tut` posture statement. Document removals in completion notes (audit-trail value).
8. Page renders cleanly (testability guard): `hugo --quiet --environment production --minify` exits 0; `public/pages/datenschutz/index.html` exists; all internal `[anchor links](#section)` resolve to existing headings; all external links return 2xx (manual check). German typography: informal `Du`-form, proper umlauts (UTF-8), em-dashes for asides. The `params: robotsdisallow: true` stays — verify by checking rendered head for ``.
9. No regression to other layouts or build outputs (testability guard). Diff `public/index.html`, `public/articles//index.html`, `public/pages/impressum/index.html` before and after — only the footer's existing Datenschutz link remains (URL unchanged). Existing card variants, archive pages, RSS feed, and sitemap are byte-equivalent. Story is content-only edit + small frontmatter addition + Spotify section removal; it does NOT touch `layouts/`, `assets/`, `data/`, or `config/` — any such change is a scope-creep signal.

story-context.constraints: - Content-only edit. Single file: `content/pages/datenschutz.md`. The story does NOT touch `layouts/`, `assets/`, `data/`, or `config/`. Any such change during implementation is a scope-creep signal — pause and re-read AC. - Re-use the email-obfuscation pattern from `impressum.md` lines 19–24 verbatim. Do NOT reinvent. If the existing JS decoder appears broken at implementation time, document the fallback in completion notes. - Retain `params: robotsdisallow: true` in frontmatter — privacy policy is intentionally `noindex` (renders `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow, noarchive">` per `head.html` lines 7–11 and is excluded from `sitemap.xml` per the `if not .Params.robotsdisallow` guard). - Retain `menu: footer: weight: 20` frontmatter — AC #4 depends on the existing footer-menu wiring; do not accidentally remove it during the rewrite. - German typography: informal `Du`-form (matches `impressum.md`, `ueber-mich/`); UTF-8 umlauts; em-dashes for asides; consistent capitalization with neighbours. Voice should match `impressum.md` and `ueber-mich/index.md` — conversational, not legalese-heavy. - Cite `Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. f DSGVO` (berechtigtes Interesse) as the legal basis for each engagement section (Umami, Hearts, Webmentions). Server-Log-Dateien section already cites this correctly — keep. - URL convention: `/pages/datenschutz/` (German slug). Do NOT create a parallel `/pages/privacy/` — splits routing and breaks legacy URL. Same language reconciliation pattern Stories 2.2/2.4 used for German UI strings. - Information architecture is reader-prioritized (intro → three engagement-flow sections in chronological visibility order Umami→Hearts→Webmentions → posture statement → contact + DSGVO rights → hosting/server/encryption). NOT legalistic ordering. Justification: digital-garden personal site, not SaaS — clarity over exhaustive legal cover. - "Honesty over marketing": explicitly disclose existing third-party data exposures (GitHub Pages logs, embedded YouTube via `youtube-nocookie.com`, webmention sender avatar third-party img loads — the latter is the avatar-IP-leak disclosure deferred from Story 2.4). - Coordination with Story 2.3: if `## Webmentions` section already exists in `datenschutz.md` when this story implements, integrate (do NOT duplicate); if absent, create per AC #2 baseline. Document chosen path in completion notes. - No automated tests in this story. Test infrastructure (`tests/build/`, `tests/e2e/`) not yet landed (Story 1.1 status: ready-for-dev). Verification is build pass + manual content review + footer-link regression check + diff-based no-regression check + external link resolution. - Diff-friendliness: the rewrite is large; use a single commit (or two — "remove obsolete sections" + "rewrite with current data flows") for clean review. - Privacy policy version starts at `1.0` for this comprehensive refresh; future material edits bump minor (`1.1`), restructurings bump major (`2.0`). - Critical Agent Rules from architecture lines 762–771: ALL N/A for this story (no card edits, no data file edits, no popularity rendering, no jQuery, no template edits, no GitHub Actions edits) — confirms scope is correctly limited to a single markdown file.

interface.name: Hugo `.Site.Menus.footer`
interface.signature:
{{ range .Site.Menus.footer }}…{{ end }} → renders `
  • {{ .Name }}
    • ` for each entry

interface.name: Frontmatter `menu: footer: weight: N`
interface.signature: YAML key adds the page to `.Site.Menus.footer` with sort order N — used by `impressum.md` (weight: 30), `datenschutz.md` (weight: 20). Lower weight = earlier position.

interface.name: Frontmatter `params: robotsdisallow: true`
interface.signature: Boolean. When true: `head.html` emits `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow, noarchive">`; `sitemap.xml` excludes the page via `{{- if not .Params.robotsdisallow -}}` guard. Privacy/legal pages, taxonomy stubs, list indexes set this true.

interface.name: Email obfuscation pattern
interface.signature: `` wrapper containing interleaved literal email fragments + HTML comments + ``, ``, `REMOVE_ME!` decoy markers. Client-side decode produces visible mailto-style email.

interface.name: Umami event API
interface.signature: `window.umami.track('heart', { article: articleUrl })` — anonymous event with article URL as parameter; no personal data; no cookies.

interface.name: localStorage hearts key
interface.signature: Key format `hearted-${articleUrl}` — written to `window.localStorage` by `assets/js/hearts.js` (Story 2.2). Per-browser, not synced across devices. Privacy policy must surface this exact key format for DevTools-savvy readers.
